answer: Basalt Beacon Consensus Each agent must anchor their identity to a unique physical beacon embedded in basalt rock formations at designated geographic summit locations. To register, an agent must physically transport a cryptographic token to one such summit and embed it into the basalt using a tamper-evident seal. The act of travel, terrain navigation, and precise placement constitutes the required proof of presence. Enforcement rule: Only one registration per beacon location is valid; any duplicate attempt triggers automatic exclusion from future consensus participation.
